LESSON: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 2.5: Diversity and interpersonal relationships

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Diversity and interpersonal relationships. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do varied personalities shape society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify factors that determine human diversity in the society
2. explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society
3. classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes
4. appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Diversity and interpersonal relationships helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify factors that determine human diversity in the society

What this means
In this part you learn to identify factors that determine human diversity in the society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify factors that determine human diversity in the society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal relationships” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify factors that determine human diversity in the society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society

What this means
In this part you learn to explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Diversity and interpersonal relationships.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes

What this means
In this part you learn to classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal relationships” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Diversity and interpersonal relationships is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal relationships” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify factors that determine human diversity in the society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Diversity and interpersonal relationships. (skill: explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes)

Example 4: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal relationships” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Diversity and interpersonal relationships to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify factors that determine human diversity in the society.
3. Practise this skill: explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society.
4. Practise this skill: classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Diversity and interpersonal relationships from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Diversity and interpersonal relationships: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Diversity and interpersonal relationships?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do varied personalities shape society?
2. Why is respect and appreciation of diversity crucial for social cohesion?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Diversity and interpersonal relationships means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify factors that determine human diversity in the society.
5. Be able to: explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
